issues.t: Engine knock and connecting rod bearing failure
issues.sym: A knocking or tapping sound from the engine that gets louder with speed, often with a flashing or steady check engine light (code P1326). It can end with the engine losing power or seizing.
issues.why: The 1.6L direct-injection engine in these years is prone to wear of the connecting rod bearings. Once a bearing wears, the engine knocks and can fail. Hyundai's engine class settlement extended the powertrain warranty on these engines to 15 years or 150,000 miles for bearing damage, provided the free knock-sensor software update (KSDS) was installed.
issues.next: If you hear knocking, stop driving hard and have a Hyundai dealer check it right away. Ask whether your VIN is covered by the extended engine warranty before paying for any repair.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearings may wear early (recall)
issues.sym: Engine knocking, a check engine light, or the engine stalling. In bad cases oil can leak onto hot parts.
issues.why: Hyundai recalled these 1.6L engines because the connecting rod bearings can wear too soon, which can damage the engine, stall it while driving, or start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-746. Under the recall, the dealer inspects the engine, installs knock-sensing software, and replaces the engine if it is damaged.

issues.t: Dual-clutch hesitation, jerking or limp mode
issues.sym: On cars with the automatic dual-clutch transmission, the car hesitates or jerks when pulling away, shifts roughly at low speed, or drops into a reduced-power limp mode with a warning light.
issues.why: The dual-clutch automatic works like two computer-controlled manual clutches. Clutch wear and control software calibration cause hesitation and shudder, especially in stop-and-go traffic. Hyundai issued software updates for the transmission.
issues.next: Ask a Hyundai dealer to check for transmission software updates and stored codes. If the shudder keeps getting worse, the clutch pack may need replacing.

issues.t: Turbo engine damage from pre-ignition (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before damage. Afterward you may notice knocking, loss of power, oil use or a check engine light.
issues.why: The original engine software on the 2013 Veloster Turbo could let fuel ignite too early under load (pre-ignition). That can crack pistons and damage the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-204. The dealer updates the engine software and inspects the engine for damage for free.

issues.t: Panoramic sunroof glass may break (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang followed by broken glass from the roof, usually while driving.
issues.why: On some early 2012 cars the panoramic sunroof assembly was weakened when it was installed at the factory, so the glass could shatter while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 12V-568 and 13V-051. The dealer inspects and repairs the sunroof for free.

issues.t: Panoramic sunroof glass shatters
issues.sym: The sunroof glass suddenly breaks with a loud pop, sometimes when parked and sometimes while driving.
issues.why: Owners have reported the moving glass panel of the panoramic sunroof shattering on its own. Hyundai extended the warranty on that glass to 10 years or 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Keep the sunshade closed if glass has cracked and get it replaced. Ask a Hyundai dealer whether the extended sunroof glass warranty covers your car.

issues.t: Clunk or click in the steering wheel
issues.sym: A clunk, click or knocking felt in the steering wheel when turning, especially at low speed or over bumps.
issues.why: The electric power steering motor connects to the steering shaft through a small rubber coupler. The coupler wears out and leaves play, which you feel and hear as a clunk.
issues.next: This is not usually dangerous, but have it checked. Replacing the rubber coupler is a fairly simple fix compared with replacing the steering column.

issues.t: Airbag light, dead horn or steering buttons from a failed clock spring
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, the horn stops working, or the steering-wheel buttons stop responding.
issues.why: The clock spring is a coiled ribbon cable behind the steering wheel that carries power to the airbag, horn and buttons. It can break over time. Hyundai extended its warranty to 15 years with unlimited miles.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read soon, since the driver airbag may not work while the light is on. Ask a dealer about the extended clock spring warranty.

issues.t: Check engine light for low fuel pressure
issues.sym: A check engine light with code P0087 (low fuel pressure), sometimes with hesitation or weak power.
issues.why: Hyundai found that the fuel feed tube can restrict fuel flow to the high-pressure fuel system. The fix is a replacement tube.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask the dealer about bulletin 15-01-023. Don't let a low fuel pressure problem go, since it can cause stalling.

issues.t: Parking brake may not hold or release (recall)
issues.sym: On manual-transmission cars the parking brake may not hold the car, or it may stay partly applied after you release it.
issues.why: Moisture and road grime could make parts of the rear parking brake mechanism stick.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 12V-567 and use a wheel chock on hills until it is fixed.

issues.t: 12-volt power outlet can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In rare cases a burning smell or heat around the accessory outlet.
issues.why: The 12-volt outlet may have been overtightened at the factory, which can disable its thermal fuse and let it overheat.
issues.next: Avoid using the outlet until the recall work (20V-393) is done at a Hyundai dealer.

issues.t: Rear parking sensor module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Parking sensor warnings, constant beeping or a blown fuse. A burning smell near the rear bumper is a warning sign.
issues.why: Water can get into the rear parking-assist circuit board and cause a short, which can lead to a fire even when the car is parked.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-132 and get it done promptly. If you smell burning, park outside away from buildings.

issues.t: ABS module can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: The ABS warning light may come on. In rare cases smoke or a burning smell comes from the engine bay, even with the car off.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak inside the anti-lock brake (ABS) control unit and cause an electrical short, which can start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-651. Park outside and away from buildings until the dealer installs the new fuse.

issues.t: Key-start cars are easy to steal
issues.sym: Signs of theft attempts such as a broken steering column cover or a damaged ignition lock, or the car being stolen.
issues.why: Veloster models started with a metal key have no engine immobilizer, and a widely shared method lets thieves start them quickly. Hyundai offers a free software upgrade that stops the engine starting unless the key fob unlocked the car.
issues.next: Have a Hyundai dealer install the free anti-theft software upgrade, and consider a steering wheel lock.

issues.t: Driver door can open in a side crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in daily driving. Some owners notice the driver door is hard to open.
issues.why: The lower window channel can damage the driver's door latch housing and lock cable in certain side impacts, letting the door open.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-311. The dealer replaces the latch and channel parts for free.

issues.t: Engine damage from faulty piston oil rings (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking, oil burning, low oil, a flashing check engine light, loss of power, or the engine stalling. Oil may leak onto hot parts.
issues.why: Some oil control rings in the 2.0L engine were not heat-treated correctly. They can break and scratch the cylinder walls, which leads to oil burning and engine damage.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-301. Under the recall, the dealer installs engine-noise monitoring software and replaces the engine if it is damaged.

issues.t: Turbo boost problems from the electric wastegate actuator
issues.sym: A check engine light, boost that surges or drops, a noise from the turbocharger, or reduced power.
issues.why: The 1.6L turbo uses an electric actuator to control boost. When it or its linkage faults, boost goes out of range and the engine limits power. Hyundai issued diagnostic bulletins for it.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer to follow the wastegate actuator bulletin before replacing the whole turbo.

issues.t: Check engine light from cold-start misfire or thermostat code
issues.sym: A check engine light with misfire codes after a cold start, or code P0128 (engine slow to warm up).
issues.why: Hyundai released engine computer updates for these codes, which could set even when no part had failed.
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether the engine software update for your car has been done before replacing parts.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump wear can cause power loss (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, rough idle, a loud misfire, and a check engine light, often at low speed.
issues.why: A valve inside the Veloster N's high-pressure fuel pump can wear and let too much fuel through, making the engine run very rich and lose power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-528. The dealer updates the engine software and replaces the pump if needed, free.

issues.t: Dual-clutch oil pump fault can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights and a fail-safe message, then after about 20–30 seconds the car loses drive power, even at speed.
issues.why: The high-pressure electric oil pump inside the 8-speed wet dual-clutch transmission can fault. The fail-safe logic then disengages the clutches.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-746. The dealer inspects the transmission, replaces it if needed, and updates the software for free.

issues.t: Blind spot warning gives false alerts
issues.sym: The blind spot light stays on or flashes with no car beside you, or misses cars that are there.
issues.why: Owners of the Veloster N report false or missed blind spot alerts, often after changing tires. Hyundai issued a software bulletin for the N's blind spot system.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the blind spot software update. Always check over your shoulder before changing lanes.
